answer: An agent marketplace serving dune restoration, trellis farming, and ocean monitoring can require every identity to lock a fixed bond for 30 days before it can submit bids, with one active bid per identity. Creating 1,000 fake agents then requires 1,000 bonds locked simultaneously. Splitting one wallet into many does not reduce that total: the attacker must tie up more capital to gain more bidding slots, paying financing costs and losing access to those funds during the lock.
